sanskrit: maṇiṃ dattvā tataḥ sītā hanūmantam athābravīt abhijñānam abhijñātam etad rāmasya tattvataḥ
english: Having given the jewel, Sītā then spoke to Hanūmān: "This token, truly known, is a recognized sign of Rāma."

sanskrit: maṇiṃ tu dṛṣṭvā rāmo vai trayāṇāṃ saṃsmariṣyati vīro jananyā mama ca rājño daśarathasya ca
english: "The hero Rāma, upon seeing this jewel, will surely remember three persons: his mother, me, and King Daśaratha."

sanskrit: sa bhūyas tvaṃ samutsāhe codito harisattama asmin kāryasamārambhe pracintaya yaduttaram
english: "And you, O best of monkeys, urged on with renewed energy, reflect upon what is best to be done in the undertaking of this task."

sanskrit: tvam asmin kāryaniryoge pramāṇaṃ harisattama tasya cintaya yo yatno duḥkhakṣayakaro bhavet
english: "You are the authority in the execution of this task, O best of monkeys; consider that effort which would bring an end to this suffering."

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratijñāya mārutir bhīmavikramaḥ śirasāvandya vaidehīṃ gamanāyopacakrame
english: Mārutī, of fearsome prowess, having agreed with "So be it," bowed his head to the daughter of Videha and prepared to depart.

sanskrit: jñātvā saṃprasthitaṃ devī vānaraṃ mārutātmajam bāṣpagadgadayā vācā maithilī vākyam abravīt
english: Knowing the son of the Wind to be ready to depart, the goddess Maithilī spoke these words in a voice choked with tears.

sanskrit: kuśalaṃ hanuman brūyāḥ sahitau rāmalakṣmaṇau sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ vṛddhān sarvāṃś ca vānarān
english: "O Hanūmān, convey my good wishes to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa together, to Sugrīva with his ministers, and to all the elder monkeys."

sanskrit: yathā ca sa mahābāhur māṃ tārayati rāghavaḥ asmād duḥkhāmbusaṃrodhāt tvaṃ samādhātum arhasi
english: "And you ought to arrange that Rāghava, that mighty-armed one, may rescue me from this flood of suffering that surrounds me."

sanskrit: jīvantīṃ māṃ yathā rāmaḥ saṃbhāvayati kīrtimān tat tvayā hanuman vācyaṃ vācā dharmam avāpnuhi
english: "That the illustrious Rāma may know me to be alive—this must be told by you, O Hanūmān; speak the word and you shall attain righteousness."

sanskrit: nityam utsāhayuktāś ca vācaḥ śrutvā mayeritāḥ vardhiṣyate dāśaratheḥ pauruṣaṃ madavāptaye
english: "Hearing these words of mine, always full of urgency, the valor of the son of Daśaratha will grow mightily for the purpose of winning me back."

sanskrit: matsaṃdeśayutā vācas tvattaḥ śrutvaiva rāghavaḥ parākramavidhiṃ vīro vidhivat saṃvidhāsyati
english: "Hearing words bearing my message from you, the heroic Rāghava will duly arrange the manner of his prowess."

sanskrit: sītāyās tad vacaḥ śrutvā hanumān mārutātmajaḥ śirasy añjalim ādhāya vākyam uttaram abravīt
english: Having heard those words of Sītā, Hanūmān, son of the Wind, placing his joined palms upon his head, spoke in reply.

sanskrit: kṣipram eṣyati kākutstho haryṛkṣapravarair vṛtaḥ yas te yudhi vijityārīñ śokaṃ vyapanayiṣyati
english: "Kākutstha will come swiftly, surrounded by the foremost of monkeys and bears, and having conquered your enemies in battle, will remove your sorrow."

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmi martyeṣu nāmareṣv asureṣu vā yas tasya vamato bāṇān sthātum utsahate 'grataḥ
english: "I see none among mortals, nor among the gods, nor among the asuras, who would dare to stand before him in the face of his discharged arrows."

sanskrit: apy arkam api parjanyam api vaivasvataṃ yamam sa hi soḍhuṃ raṇe śaktas tavahetor viśeṣataḥ
english: "He is capable of withstanding even the Sun, even Parjanya, even Yama the son of Vivasvat in battle—and especially so for your sake."

sanskrit: sa hi sāgaraparyantāṃ mahīṃ śāsitum īhate tvan nimitto hi rāmasya jayo janakanandini
english: "He desires to rule the earth to the ocean's border; the victory of Rāma has you as its occasion, O daughter of Janaka."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā samyak satyaṃ subhāṣitam jānakī bahu mene 'tha vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Having heard those words of his—perfectly true and well-spoken—Jānakī held them in high regard and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ prasthitaṃ sītā vīkṣamāṇā punaḥ punaḥ bhartuḥ snehānvitaṃ vākyaṃ sauhārdād anumānayat
english: Then Sītā, gazing again and again at the one who was about to depart, out of deep affection surmised the loving words he would carry to her husband.

sanskrit: yadi vā manyase vīra vasaikāham ariṃdama kasmiṃś cit saṃvṛte deśe viśrāntaḥ śvo gamiṣyasi
english: "Or if you think fit, O hero, O subduer of foes, remain one day in some secluded spot; rested, you may depart tomorrow."

sanskrit: mama ced alpabhāgyāyāḥ sāmnidhyāt tava vīryavān asya śokasya mahato muhūrtaṃ mokṣaṃ bhavet
english: "For through the company of you, O mighty one, even I, of little fortune, might find momentary relief from this great sorrow."

sanskrit: gate hi hariśārdūla punarāgamanāya tu prāṇānām api saṃdeho mama syān nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "For when you are gone, O tiger among monkeys, even the continuance of my life until your return will be in doubt—of this there is no question."

sanskrit: tavādarśanajaḥ śoko bhūyo māṃ paritāpayet duḥkhād duḥkhaparāmṛṣṭāṃ dīpayann iva vānara
english: "The grief born of not seeing you will afflict me further, O monkey, inflaming me who am already tormented by sorrow upon sorrow."

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca vīra saṃdehas tiṣṭhatīva mamāgrataḥ sumahāṃs tvatsahāyeṣu haryṛkṣeṣu harīśvara
english: "And this very great doubt stands before me, O hero, O lord of monkeys, concerning the monkey and bear troops who are your allies."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu khalu duṣpāraṃ tariṣyanti mahodadhim tāni haryṛkṣasainyāni tau vā naravarātmajau
english: "How indeed shall those armies of monkeys and bears cross the great, impassable ocean? Or how shall those two sons of the noblest of men?"

sanskrit: trayāṇām eva bhūtānāṃ sāgarasyeha laṅghane śaktiḥ syād vainateyasya tava vā mārutasya vā
english: "Among living beings, only three have the power to leap over this ocean: Vainateya, you yourself, or the Wind."

sanskrit: tad asmin kāryaniryoge vīraivaṃ duratikrame kiṃ paśyasi samādhānaṃ tvaṃ hi kāryavidāṃ varaḥ
english: "So in the execution of this task, O hero, so hard to accomplish, what solution do you see? You are the foremost among those who understand what must be done."

sanskrit: kāmam asya tvam evaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane paryāptaḥ paravīraghna yaśasyas te balodayaḥ
english: "Certainly you alone are sufficient for the accomplishment of this task, O slayer of enemy heroes; your growth in power is glorious."

sanskrit: balaiḥ samagrair yadi māṃ rāvaṇaṃ jitya saṃyuge vijayī svapuraṃ yāyāt tat tu me syād yaśaskaram
english: "But if the victorious Rāghava were to conquer Rāvaṇa in battle with his full forces and then return to his own city with me—that would bring him glory."

sanskrit: balais tu saṃkulāṃ kṛtvā laṅkāṃ parabalārdanaḥ māṃ nayed yadi kākutsthas tat tasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet
english: "If Kākutstha, the crusher of enemy armies, were to fill Laṅkā with troops and then lead me away—that would be befitting of him."

sanskrit: tad yathā tasya vikrāntam anurūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ bhaved āhava śūrasya tathā tvam upapādaya
english: "Therefore arrange it so that the valor of that great-souled hero in battle may be in keeping with his nature as a warrior."

sanskrit: tad arthopahitaṃ vākyaṃ sahitaṃ hetusaṃhitam niśamya hanumāñ śeṣaṃ vākyam uttaram abravīt
english: Having heard those words—purposeful, coherent, and supported by reasoning—Hanūmān spoke further in reply.

sanskrit: devi haryṛkṣasainyānām īśvaraḥ plavatāṃ varaḥ sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṃpannas tavārthe kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: "O goddess, Sugrīva, lord of the armies of monkeys and bears, the best among those who leap, endowed with true strength, is firmly resolved for your sake."

sanskrit: sa vānarasahasrāṇāṃ koṭībhir abhisaṃvṛtaḥ kṣipram eṣyati vaidehi rākṣasānāṃ nibarhaṇaḥ
english: "Surrounded by tens of millions of thousands of monkeys, that destroyer of rākṣasas will come swiftly, O Vaidehī."

sanskrit: tasya vikramasaṃpannāḥ sattvavanto mahābalāḥ manaḥsaṃkalpasaṃpātā nideśe harayaḥ sthitāḥ
english: "His monkeys, endowed with prowess, full of courage, of great strength, who fly as swift as thought's resolve, stand ready at his command."

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ nopari nādhastān na tiryak sajjate gatiḥ na ca karmasu sīdanti mahatsv amitatejasaḥ
english: "Their motion is not obstructed above, below, or sideways; of unlimited splendor, they do not falter in great deeds."

sanskrit: asakṛt tair mahotsahaiḥ sasāgaradharādharā pradakṣiṇīkṛtā bhūmir vāyumārgānusāribhiḥ
english: "By those ones of vast energy, who travel the path of the wind, the earth together with its ocean and mountains has been circumambulated more than once."

sanskrit: madviśiṣṭāś ca tulyāś ca santi tatra vanaukasaḥ mattaḥ pratyavaraḥ kaś cin nāsti sugrīvasaṃnidhau
english: "There are forest-dwellers there who are both superior to me and equal to me; there is none inferior to me in Sugrīva's presence."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tāvad iha prāptaḥ kiṃ punas te mahābalāḥ na hi prakṛṣṭāḥ preṣyante preṣyante hītare janāḥ
english: "I, who am merely the least, have arrived here—how much more so those of great strength! For it is not the foremost who are sent as messengers; it is the lesser ones who are sent."

sanskrit: tad alaṃ paritāpena devi śoko vyapaitu te ekotpātena te laṅkām eṣyanti hariyūthapāḥ
english: "Therefore enough of this anguish, O goddess; let your sorrow depart. With a single bound the leaders of monkey troops will come to Laṅkā."

sanskrit: mama pṛṣṭhagatau tau ca candrasūryāv ivoditau tvatsakāśaṃ mahāsattvau nṛsiṃhāv āgamiṣyataḥ
english: "And those two, like the risen sun and moon, those two beings of great nature, those two lion-men, riding upon my back, will come to your presence."

sanskrit: tau hi vīrau naravarau sahitau rāmalakṣmaṇau āgamya nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ sāyakair vidhamiṣyataḥ
english: "For those two heroes, those best of men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa together, coming to the city of Laṅkā, will scatter it with their arrows."

sanskrit: sagaṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ hatvā rāghavo raghunandanaḥ tvām ādāya varārohe svapuraṃ pratiyāsyati
english: "Having slain Rāvaṇa together with his followers, the joy of the Raghu clan, Rāghava, will return to his own city taking you with him, O lady of beautiful thighs."

sanskrit: tad āśvasihi bhadraṃ te bhava tvaṃ kālakāṅkṣiṇī nacirād drakṣyase rāmaṃ prajvajantam ivānilam
english: "So take heart, may good fortune be yours; be patient, waiting for the right moment. Before long you will see Rāma blazing like fire in the wind."

sanskrit: nihate rākṣasendre ca saputrāmātyabāndhave tvaṃ sameṣyasi rāmeṇa śaśāṅkeneva rohiṇī
english: "When the lord of rākṣasas has been slain along with his sons, ministers, and kinsmen, you will be united with Rāma as Rohiṇī with the moon."

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ tvaṃ devi śokasya pāraṃ yāsyasi maithili rāvaṇaṃ caiva rāmeṇa nihataṃ drakṣyase 'cirāt
english: "O goddess, O Maithilī, you will quickly reach the far shore of sorrow, and before long you will see Rāvaṇa slain by Rāma."

sanskrit: evam āśvasya vaidehīṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ gamanāya matiṃ kṛtvā vaidehīṃ punar abravīt
english: Having thus reassured Vaidehī, Hanūmān, son of the Wind, having resolved to depart, spoke to Vaidehī once more.

sanskrit: tam arighnaṃ kṛtātmānaṃ kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi rāghavam lakṣmaṇaṃ ca dhanuṣpāṇiṃ laṅkādvāram upasthitam
english: "You will soon see that slayer of enemies, the self-mastered Rāghava, and Lakṣmaṇa bow in hand, standing at the gate of Laṅkā."

sanskrit: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhān vīrān siṃhaśārdūlavikramān vānarān vāraṇendrābhān kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi saṃgatān
english: "You will quickly see those heroic monkeys assembled—armed with claws and fangs, striding like lions and tigers, resembling lordly elephants."

sanskrit: śailāmbudanikāśānāṃ laṅkāmalayasānuṣu nardatāṃ kapimukhyānām ārye yūthāny anekaśaḥ
english: "O noble lady, you will see the many troops of the chief monkeys—resembling mountains and rain-clouds—roaring upon the slopes of Laṅkā's Malaya peaks."

sanskrit: sa tu marmaṇi ghoreṇa tāḍito manmatheṣuṇā na śarma labhate rāmaḥ siṃhārdita iva dvipaḥ
english: "And Rāma, struck to the vitals by the terrible arrow of the god of love, finds no peace—like an elephant tormented by a lion."

sanskrit: mā rudo devi śokena mā bhūt te manaso 'priyam śacīva pathyā śakreṇa bhartrā nāthavatī hy asi
english: "Do not weep, O goddess, from grief; let there be nothing displeasing to your heart. Like Śacī blessed with Śakra, you have a lord and protector as your husband."

sanskrit: rāmād viśiṣṭaḥ ko 'nyo 'sti kaś cit saumitriṇā samaḥ agnimārutakalpau tau bhrātarau tava saṃśrayau
english: "Who else is superior to Rāma? Who is equal to the son of Sumitrā? Those two brothers, equal to fire and wind, are your refuge."

sanskrit: nāsmiṃś ciraṃ vatsyasi devi deśe rakṣogaṇair adhyuṣito 'tiraudre na te cirād āgamanaṃ priyasya kṣamasva matsaṃgamakālamātram
english: "You will not dwell long in this place, O goddess, this dreadful one inhabited by hordes of rākṣasas. The coming of your beloved will not be long delayed. Endure only the duration of the time until we meet again."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya vāyusūnor mahātmanaḥ uvācātmahitaṃ vākyaṃ sītā surasutopamā
english: Having heard those words of the great-souled son of the Wind, Sītā, who resembles the daughter of a god, spoke words conducive to her own welfare.

sanskrit: tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā priyavaktāraṃ saṃprahṛṣyāmi vānara ardhasaṃjātasasyeva vṛṣṭiṃ prāpya vasuṃdharā
english: "Upon seeing you, O monkey, who speak such dear words, I rejoice greatly—like the earth receiving rain when the crop is half-grown."

sanskrit: yathā taṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ gātraiḥ śokābhikarśitaiḥ saṃspṛśeyaṃ sakāmāhaṃ tathā kuru dayāṃ mayi
english: "Arrange it, out of compassion for me, that I may embrace that tiger among men with these limbs emaciated by grief—this is my desire."

sanskrit: abhijñānaṃ ca rāmasya dattaṃ harigaṇottama kṣiptām īṣikāṃ kākasya kopād ekākṣiśātanīm
english: "And a token of recognition from Rāma has been given to me, O foremost of monkey troops: the blade of grass thrown in anger at the crow that gouged out one of its eyes."

sanskrit: manaḥśilāyās tikalo gaṇḍapārśve niveśitaḥ tvayā pranaṣṭe tilake taṃ kila smartum arhasi
english: "A mark of red mineral dye was placed on my cheek; he should indeed remember that mark, which has now faded, O monkey."

sanskrit: sa vīryavān kathaṃ sītāṃ hṛtāṃ samanumanyate vasantīṃ rakṣasāṃ madhye mahendravaruṇopama
english: "How can that mighty one, equal to Mahendra and Varuṇa, tolerate Sītā, who has been abducted, dwelling in the midst of rākṣasas?"

sanskrit: eṣa cūḍāmaṇir divyo mayā suparirakṣitaḥ etaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahṛṣyāmi vyasane tvām ivānagha
english: "This divine crest-jewel has been carefully guarded by me. Upon seeing it I rejoice—as I rejoice at seeing you, O sinless one, in my misfortune."

sanskrit: eṣa niryātitaḥ śrīmān mayā te vārisaṃbhavaḥ ataḥ paraṃ na śakṣyāmi jīvituṃ śokalālasā
english: "This auspicious jewel, born of water, is hereby surrendered by me to you. Beyond this I shall not be able to live, consumed with longing in my grief."

sanskrit: asahyāni ca duḥkhāni vācaś ca hṛdayacchidaḥ rākṣasīnāṃ sughorāṇāṃ tvatkṛte marṣayāmy aham
english: "I endure unbearable sufferings and words that pierce the heart from those terrifying rākṣasī women—all for your sake."

sanskrit: dhārayiṣyāmi māsaṃ tu jīvitaṃ śatrusūdana māsād ūrdhvaṃ na jīviṣye tvayā hīnā nṛpātmaja
english: "I shall sustain my life, O slayer of enemies, for one month; beyond one month I shall not live, O son of a king, separated from you."

sanskrit: ghoro rākṣasarājo 'yaṃ dṛṣṭiś ca na sukhā mayi tvāṃ ca śrutvā vipadyantaṃ na jīveyam ahaṃ kṣaṇam
english: "This rākṣasa king is terrible, and his gaze upon me brings no ease; and if I were to hear of your falling into misfortune, I could not live another moment."

sanskrit: vaidehyā vacanaṃ śrutvā karuṇaṃ sāśrubhāṣitam athābravīn mahātejā hanumān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Having heard the compassion-stirring words of Vaidehī, spoken amid tears, then the greatly resplendent Hanūmān, son of the Wind, spoke.

sanskrit: tvacchokavimukho rāmo devi satyena te śape rāme śokābhibhūte tu lakṣmaṇaḥ paritapyate
english: "Rāma is free of sorrow for none but you, O goddess—I swear to you in truth. And when Rāma is overwhelmed with grief, Lakṣmaṇa too burns with anguish."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā kathaṃ cid bhavatī na kālaḥ pariśocitum imaṃ muhūrtaṃ duḥkhānām antaṃ drakṣyasi bhāmini
english: "You have been found, somehow. This is not the time for lamenting. In this very moment you will see the end of your sorrows, O passionate lady."

sanskrit: tāv ubhau puruṣavyāghrau rājaputrāv aninditau tvaddarśanakṛtotsāhau laṅkāṃ bhasmīkariṣyataḥ
english: "Those two tigers among men, those two blameless princes, their enthusiasm kindled by the sight of you, will reduce Laṅkā to ashes."

sanskrit: hatvā tu samare krūraṃ rāvaṇaṃ saha bāndhavam rāghavau tvāṃ viśālākṣi svāṃ purīṃ prāpayiṣyataḥ
english: "Having slain the cruel Rāvaṇa together with his kinsmen in battle, both Rāghavas will bring you to your own city, O wide-eyed one."

sanskrit: yat tu rāmo vijānīyād abhijñānam anindite prītisaṃjananaṃ tasya bhūyas tvaṃ dātum arhasi
english: "But whatever token Rāma might recognize, O blameless one, that which will generate delight in him—you ought to give yet another such."

sanskrit: sābravīd dattam eveha mayābhijñānam uttamam etad eva hi rāmasya dṛṣṭvā matkeśabhūṣaṇam śraddheyaṃ hanuman vākyaṃ tava vīra bhaviṣyati
english: She said: "The finest token has already been given by me here. For upon seeing this hair ornament of mine, O Hanūmān, your words, O hero, will be held credible by Rāma."

sanskrit: sa taṃ maṇivaraṃ gṛhya śrīmān plavagasattamaḥ praṇamya śirasā devīṃ gamanāyopacakrame
english: Taking that finest of jewels, the auspicious best of leapers bowed his head to the goddess and prepared to depart.

sanskrit: tam utpātakṛtotsāham avekṣya haripuṃgavam vardhamānaṃ mahāvegaṃ uvāca janakātmajā aśrupūrṇamukhī dīnā bāṣpagadgadayā girā
english: Beholding that bull among monkeys whose enthusiasm had risen for the leap, who was growing in his great velocity, the daughter of Janaka, wretched, her face filled with tears, spoke in a voice choked with sobs.

sanskrit: hanūman siṃhasaṃkāśau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ sarvān brūyā anāmayam
english: "Hanūmān, convey my good health to the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who resemble lions, and to Sugrīva with his ministers—to all of them."

sanskrit: yathā ca sa mahābāhur māṃ tārayati rāghavaḥ asmād duḥkhāmbusaṃrodhāt tat samādhātum arhasi
english: "And you must arrange that Rāghava, that mighty-armed one, may rescue me from this flood of sorrow that engulfs me."

sanskrit: imaṃ ca tīvraṃ mama śokavegaṃ rakṣobhir ebhiḥ paribhartsanaṃ ca brūyās tu rāmasya gataḥ samīpaṃ śivaś ca te 'dhvāstu haripravīra
english: "And this fierce surge of my sorrow, and the threats made by these rākṣasas—convey all this when you have come into Rāma's presence. May your path be auspicious, O hero among monkeys."

sanskrit: sa rājaputryā prativeditārthaḥ kapiḥ kṛtārthaḥ parihṛṣṭacetāḥ tad alpaśeṣaṃ prasamīkṣya kāryaṃ diśaṃ hy udīcīṃ manasā jagāma
english: That monkey, informed of the princess's wishes, his task accomplished, his heart overjoyed, surveying the little that remained to be done, turned his mind northward.

sanskrit: sa ca vāgbhiḥ praśastābhiḥ gamiṣyan pūjitas tayā tasmād deśād apakramya cintayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Honored by her with words of praise as he was about to depart, the monkey withdrew from that place and began to reflect.

sanskrit: alpaśeṣam idaṃ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭeyam asitekṣaṇā trīn upāyān atikramya caturtha iha dṛśyate
english: "This task is little short of complete; the dark-eyed lady has been seen. Passing over three of the four means of policy, a fourth presents itself here."

sanskrit: na sāma rakṣaḥsu guṇāya kalpate na danam arthopaciteṣu vartate na bhedasādhyā baladarpitā janāḥ parākramas tv eṣa mameha rocate
english: "Conciliation avails nothing with rākṣasas; gifts do not apply among those who dwell in accumulated wealth; those intoxicated with the power of their army cannot be won over by sowing dissension. But valor—this is what pleases me here."

sanskrit: na cāsya kāryasya parākramād ṛte viniścayaḥ kaś cid ihopapadyate hṛtapravīrās tu raṇe hi rākṣasāḥ kathaṃ cid īyur yad ihādya mārdavam
english: "No resolution of this task is possible here without valor. For the rākṣasas, their champions slain in battle, might perhaps somehow come to a state of softness."

sanskrit: kārye karmaṇi nirdiṣṭo yo bahūny api sādhayet pūrvakāryavirodhena sa kāryaṃ kartum arhati
english: "One who is appointed to a specific task but who might accomplish many things without obstructing the primary task—he may indeed perform those things."

sanskrit: na hy ekaḥ sādhako hetuḥ svalpasyāpīha karmaṇaḥ yo hy arthaṃ bahudhā veda sa samartho 'rthasādhane
english: "For no single means alone accomplishes even the slightest task here. One who knows a purpose from many angles is capable of its accomplishment."

sanskrit: ihaiva tāvat kṛtaniścayo hy ahaṃ yadi vrajeyaṃ plavageśvarālayam parātmasaṃmarda viśeṣatattvavit tataḥ kṛtaṃ syān mama bhartṛśāsanam
english: "Having resolved here and now—if I were to go back to the abode of the lord of monkeys, I, who know the essence of the crushing contest between self and enemy, then my master's command would be considered fulfilled."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu khalv adya bhavet sukhāgataṃ prasahya yuddhaṃ mama rākṣasaiḥ saha tathaiva khalv ātmabalaṃ ca sāravat samānayen māṃ ca raṇe daśānanaḥ
english: "How then might a battle forced upon me today with the rākṣasas come about pleasingly? And in the same way, might the ten-faced one measure up in combat to my own essential strength?"

sanskrit: idam asya nṛśaṃsasya nandanopamam uttamam vanaṃ netramanaḥkāntaṃ nānādrumalatāyutam
english: "This finest grove of that cruel one, comparable to the garden of the gods, pleasing to the eye and heart, filled with many kinds of trees and creepers—"

sanskrit: idaṃ vidhvaṃsayiṣyāmi śuṣkaṃ vanam ivānalaḥ asmin bhagne tataḥ kopaṃ kariṣyati sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: "—this I will destroy, as fire destroys a dry forest. When this is destroyed, Rāvaṇa will then be moved to anger."

sanskrit: tato mahat sāśvamahārathadvipaṃ balaṃ samāneṣv api rākṣasādhipaḥ triśūlakālāyasapaṭṭiśāyudhaṃ tato mahad yuddhaṃ idaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Then the lord of rākṣasas will dispatch a great force complete with horses, great chariots, and elephants, armed with tridents, iron bars, and battle-axes—and then this great battle will ensue."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu taiḥ saṃyati caṇḍavikramaiḥ sametya rakṣobhir asaṃgavikramaḥ nihatya tad rāvaṇacoditaṃ balaṃ sukhaṃ gamiṣyāmi kapīśvarālayam
english: "But I, meeting those rākṣasas of fierce valor in combat, of unimpeded prowess, having slain that army dispatched by Rāvaṇa, will depart gladly to the abode of the lord of monkeys."

sanskrit: tato mārutavat kruddho mārutir bhīmavikramaḥ ūruvegena mahatā drumān kṣeptum athārabhat
english: Then Mārutī, angry as the wind itself, of fearsome prowess, with the great force of his thighs, began to hurl down the trees.

sanskrit: tatas tad dhanumān vīro babhañja pramadāvanam mattadvijasamāghuṣṭaṃ nānādrumalatāyutam
english: Then the heroic Hanūmān broke apart that pleasure grove, resounding with the calls of intoxicated birds, filled with many kinds of trees and creepers.

sanskrit: tad vanaṃ mathitair vṛkṣair bhinnaiś ca salilāśayaiḥ cūrṇitaiḥ parvatāgraiś ca babhūvāpriyadarśanam
english: That grove, with its trees torn up and its pools broken apart and its hilltops pulverized, became a sight unpleasant to behold.

sanskrit: latāgṛhaiś citragṛhaiś ca nāśitair mahoragair vyālamṛgaiś ca nirdhutaiḥ śilāgṛhair unmathitais tathā gṛhaiḥ pranaṣṭarūpaṃ tad abhūn mahad vanam
english: With its bower-houses of creepers and its painted houses destroyed, its great serpents and wild beasts driven out, its stone-houses overturned and its buildings shattered, that great grove lost all semblance of its former form.

sanskrit: sa tasya kṛtvārthapater mahākapir mahad vyalīkaṃ manaso mahātmanaḥ yuyutsur eko bahubhir mahābalaiḥ śriyā jvalaṃs toraṇam āśritaḥ kapiḥ
english: That great monkey, having done great offense to the heart of that wealthy lord, blazing with splendor, desiring single combat with many of great strength, took his stand at the gateway.
